doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Drugs and the House of Correction
title: A week with Billie Holiday and the House of Correction in 1952
summary: Billie Holiday fires Ware and a drummer for using sticks; drugs then put Ware in the House of Correction for 1952.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Well, I did that up until about 1950 -- that was about a year -- '49-50 was my hardest time, and the guy offered me a job with Billie Holiday -- a little club on the north side; a trio -- she had a piano player, Carl Drinkard, and yeah, I want to make it. We got a drummer out of Chicago -- a beautiful drummer, a white dude named Guy Devereaux -- he loved Ike Day and played just like him, and I don't know whether he thought he
thought he was supposed to play with sticks behind Billy, but he did ...

She said, 'No sticks ... brushes.' Wam, Wam, she Naturally, wouldn't fired me and him. Now she had to get rid of the piano player. But that was the first time I worked with her. And then I had to pay my dues. Drugs caused me to go to the House of Correction in Chicago, and I spent all of 1952 in there.
